10.1002_adfm.78173: Revealing Solvation Effects by Cryo-EM This cover artwork features Lord Er-lang from Journey to the West, one of China's Four Great Classical Novels. His renowned third-eye power, symbolic of robust discernment to reveal underlying realities, renders him a figurative counterpart to Cryo-EM. Just as his third-eye vision breaks past illusions, Cryo-EM electron beams enable high-resolution observation of nanocrystals generated by solvation effects in battery electrolytes. Besides, the shrimp soldiers symbolize solvent molecules, while the crab generals represent salt anions; their competition for Na+ vividly illustrates the solvation effect in the electrolyte. This artistic depiction directly conveys the core message of the work: the use of Cryo-EM to resolve the solvation structure of electrolytes, thereby opening a new methodological avenue for electrolyte research and offering fresh insights for future screening of battery electrolytes. More details can be found in the Research Article by Zhengkun Xie, Weihua Chen, and co-workers (DOI: 10.1002/adfm.76624).
10.1002_tcr.70152: For more than 50 years, nickel foam electrodes have served in electrosynthesis as powerful and readily available electrode materials. Due to their inexpensive nature and easy handling, they have been widely employed. Their application as an active anode material, which generates a conductive and insoluble layer of NiOOH in alkaline media, gives access to a selective oxidizing system. While using NiOOH anodes as an electrocatalyst has already emerged in the past and was rediscovered lately, the use of nickel foam electrodes as a highly active cathode material for the reduction of organic compounds has strongly evolved only within the last decade. Electroreductions on nickel foam can be carried out in both alkaline and acidic media, as well as under protic and aprotic conditions, enabling a broad range of transformations. The affordability, high electrical conductivity, large electrode surface area, and specific electrocatalytic features are in combination unique and unmatched by any other electrode material. The developments and, in particular, recent breakthroughs for this electrode material in electro-organic synthesis are surveyed.
10.1016_j.esci.2026.100617: Aqueous ammonium-ion batteries (AAIBs) offer a sustainable energy storage pathway but are limited by sluggish ion transport and structural instability. Here, we report a polymer-functionalization strategy by intercalating poly(2-ethyl-2-oxazoline) (EtOx) into tunnel-structured V 6 O 13 to form EtOx-V 6 O 13 . The intercalated polymer not only expands and stabilizes diffusion channels but also introduces abundant carbonyl groups that form N–H···O=C hydrogen bonds with . These interactions establish a dynamic hydrogen-bond network that enables relay-like transport via continuous bond breaking and reformation, thereby significantly lowering migration barriers and facilitating rapid ion conduction. Notably, this process involves the coordinated movement of intact ions through successive docking at carbonyl sites, distinguishing it from classical proton hopping. The synergistic effects of structural expansion and hydrogen-bond-mediated transportation also buffer lattice strain and enhance structural integrity during cycling. As a result, EtOx-V 6 O 13 -0.4 delivers 227.8 mAh g −1 at 1 A g −1 , retains 102.6 mAh g −1 at 20 A g −1 , and achieves 90.2% capacity retention over 5000 cycles. A full cell with MnO 2 exhibits 146.9 mAh g −1 at 0.1 A g −1 and an energy density of 110.2 Wh kg −1 . This work highlights polymer-functionalized tunnel oxides as an effective platform for hydrogen-bond-mediated ion transport in AAIBs.
10.1016_j.tsep.2026.104662: During electrode calendering, mismatched mechanical responses across scales in heterogeneous material systems under nonuniform stress fields lead to coordinated macro-scale and micro-scale defect formation. Conventional heated calendering heats the coating via hot rollers while the current collector (the structural backbone) remains near ambient temperature. This limits the defect-suppression capability of the temperature field. This study proposes electromagnetic induction heating of the current collector as the heat source to achieve integral electrode heating during calendering. Synchronous thermal softening of the heterogeneous constituents should better suppress defect formation. A thermal simulation model was established to clarify the induction heating mechanism of the current collector and the evolution of temperature gradients within the coating. The feasibility of temperature regulation in the proposed process was validated. The effects of coil geometry and current parameters on the target temperature distribution of the current collector were examined. The relationship between coating structural densification and heat-transfer behavior was clarified. In-situ hot compression experiments demonstrate that thermally induced softening enhances electrode compaction efficiency and electrical conductivity. The resistance of NMC cathode during hot compression process at 140 ℃ decreased from a maximum of 1.75 Ω to 0.14 Ω compared to 22 ℃. This work proposes a new approach to temperature control in electrode heated calendering and advances the understanding of Li-ion battery electrode forming processes.
10.1038_s41467-025-63450-x: Co-electrolysis of CO 2 with simple N-species is an appealing route to sustainable fabrication of C-N bond containing products. A prominent challenge in this direction is to promote the C-N coupling step in place of the established CO 2 reduction pathways. This can be particularly difficult when relying on solution-based species (e.g., NH 3 ) to intercept intermediates that are continually being reduced on heterogeneous catalyst surfaces. In light of this, we introduce oxy-reductive pulsed electrocatalysis as a tool for C-N bond formation. The reaction routes opened through this method involve both partial reduction and partial oxidation of separate reactants on the same catalyst surface in parallel to co-adsorb their activated intermediates proximal to one another. Using CO 2 and NH 3 as model reactants, the end result is an enhancement of selectivity and formation rates for C-N bond containing products (urea, formamide, acetamide, methylamine) by factors of 3-20 as compared to static electrolysis in otherwise identical conditions. An array of operando measurements is carried out to pinpoint the key factors behind this performance enhancement. Finally, the oxy-reductive coupling strategy is extended to additional carbon and nitrogen reactants and is further applied to C-S coupling.
10.1038_s41538-026-01175-x: Polymeric tea bags act as dynamic vectors for micro-particle shedding and chemical leaching, raising public health concerns as global tea consumption rises. This study quantified microplastics (MPs), bisphenol A (BPA), and phthalate esters (PAEs) in infusions prepared from 14 bagged and 14 bulk tea brands, and modeled the associated health risks. Following a controlled brewing simulation (95 °C, 3 min), MPs were characterized by ATR-FTIR and chemical leaching was quantified by GC-MS/MS. Plastic tea bags released substantially more MPs (555–2498 particles/cup) than bulk tea (0.3–2.4 MP/cup). Debris exceeding 100 µm from tea bags consisted exclusively of polyamide (PA) fibers, consistent with hydrolytic degradation of the bag material, whereas bulk tea showed a heterogeneous polymer profile (PE, PP, PET, and PA) dominated by fragments (70–80%), reflecting background environmental and industrial contamination. Although cumulative Hazard Index values remained below the risk threshold (HI <1), BPA intake from bagged tea reached 21.7% of the EFSA tolerable daily intake. These findings indicate that polymeric tea bags act as active vectors for particulate and chemical pollutants, supporting a shift toward bulk tea consumption and stricter regulatory oversight of food-contact packaging materials.
